title: Learning something new: six opinions

script.text: When I bought a guitar, I thought I'd practise for hours every weekend. That lasted two weeks. So I tried ten minutes every day, even when my fingers hurt. A year later I can play twelve songs, though I still make mistakes every evening. My brother has one long session on Sundays and nothing else, and he's still on the same three chords.

I'd never have kept going with Spanish at home with a video app, because my motivation lasted two weeks each time. Then I joined an evening class with eight strangers. I was embarrassed by my accent at first, but theirs were worse, and we laughed. When I felt like skipping a lesson, I remembered that the group would ask where I was. Last week I ordered a whole dinner in Spanish.

My first programme crashed eleven times in a row, and I nearly gave up. My teacher said every mistake was telling me what I'd misunderstood, so I wrote them all in a notebook and read it every day for a month. It turned out to be the most useful book I own. Now, when something goes wrong, I'm almost pleased.

My daughters laughed when I said I wanted to learn to swim at fifty-two. For years I was too embarrassed to mention it, because beginners are supposed to be children. Then I found an instructor with pupils from six to seventy-eight. I'm slow, and I always will be, but last summer I swam across a lake.

Photography began as my hobby on holiday. Friends started asking me to take pictures at their weddings, and a local magazine found my website. Two years later I left my office job. People ask whether I learnt from video lessons. A few, but mostly I took one picture every day.

I watched hundreds of cooking video lessons before I made bread. In every one it looked easy. My first loaf was like a brick, but everybody makes mistakes. Then my neighbour, who bakes professionally, stood next to me for one afternoon and showed me how the dough should feel. I learnt more in three hours than in all my evenings online.

options: Beginners should not be embarrassed about their level.
Learning in a group keeps you motivated.
A hobby can turn into a job.
Video lessons are not enough to learn a practical skill.
Mistakes are a useful part of learning.
A little practice every day works better than long sessions once a week.
You are never too old to learn something new.
discuss: Which of the six speakers would you most like to learn from? Why?
What is the most difficult thing you have ever learnt? How did you manage it?
Do you prefer learning alone, with a teacher or in a group?
